title: Notification message v1
description: What CORE hands to a channel adapter. This is the contract a provider integration is written against, and it is deliberately not a serialisation of the internal notification row: the row carries claim tokens, attempt counters and error text that no adapter may see. Every field here is either addressing, a rendered human-readable message, or the small set of named event facts the message was rendered from. Adding a field is a contract change; renaming one is a breaking change.

notification_id.description: CORE's identifier for this notification. Stable across attempts, so an operator can take it from a provider console back to CORE.

idempotency_key.description: Derived from the event and the recipient (`<event_id>:<recipient_id>`), so every attempt at the same notification carries the same key and a provider that honours idempotency keys collapses a repeat. CORE does not assume any provider does: the key is offered, never relied on.

channel.description: Which channel the adapter is being asked to use. An adapter is registered for exactly one channel and must refuse anything else.

address.description: The verified address for that channel, resolved once at fan-out time and frozen. Never re-resolved per attempt: a retry must go where the notification was created for.

template.description: Which message this is, from a closed set. An adapter may use it to pick a provider-side template; it must not need to parse the body to find out what happened.

subject.description: Present for channels that have a subject line, null for channels that do not (telegram, phone).

body.description: The rendered message. Rendered from named event fields by CORE, never from a dump of an internal record.

data.description: The named event facts the body was rendered from, so an adapter using a provider-side template can rebuild the same message without re-deriving anything. Only the fields listed here are ever included, and a field is absent rather than null when the event did not carry it.

reference.description: What the message calls the work: MARKET's opaque order reference when the event carries one, otherwise the CORE fulfillment id. CORE holds no customer identity behind that reference (see ROADMAP D-7).

reason.description: The domain reason code the event carried. A code support can look up, not prose.

settlement_state.description: The settlement state at closure, verbatim from the event. Absent when the event carried none.

financial_decision_required.description: True when money is still held and no capture-or-release decision has been made. A message rendered from such an event MUST NOT be phrased as a refund or a final settlement, because no such decision has happened (ROADMAP D-6).

subscription_id.description: Subscription the message is about, for subscription templates.

period_id.description: The billing period that went unpaid, when the event carries it.

amount_minor.description: Amount in minor units exactly as the ledger holds it. Not divided and not locale-formatted: CORE does not know the recipient's locale, and a misplaced decimal point in a payment demand is worse than an unglamorous number.

attempt.description: Which attempt this is, starting at 1. Present so an adapter can log it; the retry decision belongs to CORE, never to the adapter.

examples.subject: Your request is complete
examples.body: Request order-8821 has been completed. The authorised payment was charged.

examples.subject: Your request could not be completed
examples.body: Request order-9910 could not be completed (reason: move_job_failed). A payment amount is held pending review; no refund or charge has been decided yet.
